newsitem.title: QATAR: India to attend MENA summit - Indian MP.
newsitem.headline: India to attend MENA summit - Indian MP.

text.p: An Indian parliamentarian said his country would participate in the controversial Middle East and North Africa (MENA) economic summit in Qatar later this year.

The regional summit, due to be held in November, traditionally includes Arab states and Israel. But some Arab countries have threatened to boycott the meeting over the deadlocked Middle East peace process.

"We attended the Cairo summit (the 1996 MENA summit) at the ministerial level and we hope to do the same if invited by the host country," Congress party parliamentarian K. M. Khan said on Wednesday. The Congress party supports Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's centre-left United Front government.
"The MENA summit may well be the turning point in the stalled Arab-Israeli peace process," Khan said.
"The conference will provide a forum for Arabs to put forward their concerns and point of view and help work out answers," he told reporters during a two-day visit to Qatar.

Khan said that during his visit he met with Qatar's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmad Abdullah al-Mahmood and other officials and found Qatari leaders unmoved by pressure from some countries to cancel the November 16-18 conference.
"They are going ahead with preparations at full steam to make the event a success," he said.
